author: NorthEast News Desk
body: West Place Animal Sanctuary is marking 20 years of caring for injured, neglected and abused farm animals in Tiverton. Founder Wendy Taylor left her law practice to build the nonprofit after nine of her pets died in a house fire, turning that loss into a long-term rescue mission.

The sanctuary occupies eight acres of historic farmland and houses a varied group that can include cows, pigs, alpacas, sheep, goats, emus, peafowl, chickens, turtles and koi. Many arrive through animal-control officers, wildlife organizations or groups such as the Rhode Island SPCA and MSPCA when an ordinary dog-and-cat shelter cannot take them.

Taylor told Ocean State Media that the organization concentrates on animals facing the greatest need. When a privately owned goat or sheep is healthy but needs a new home, staff may help arrange placement elsewhere so the sanctuary can preserve space and resources for urgent cases.

West Place says it has saved thousands of animals since opening. Its anniversary also highlights a specialized gap in the regional shelter system: farm animals seized by police or removed from neglect often require land, equipment and expertise that municipal facilities do not have. The Tiverton operation has become one of the places authorities call when those cases arise.
dek: The eight-acre sanctuary grew from founder Wendy Taylor’s personal tragedy into a refuge serving abused and neglected animals across the region.
headline: Tiverton’s West Place marks 20 years rescuing farm animals
